clue.text: Split inspires female, transformed

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the word for split draws the female inside itself

parts.note: to rend is to split or tear
a ewe is a female sheep

explanation.surface: Something broken apart somehow brings a woman to life and changes her.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspires looks like encouragement, but read literally it means breathing in, which is how one word ends up inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something made new again has been transformed.

clue.text: Denial after returning clothes mostly made of divisive material

indicators.note: going back the way it came, so the word for after is read right to left
to clothe something is to wrap it up, so the reversed word goes around the fur
most but not all of the word, so FUR loses its last letter

parts.note: after = later, read backwards
fur is a material that divides opinion; mostly leaves FU

explanation.surface: A garment gets rejected because it is made of a controversial fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divisive material' is a cryptic way to describe fur, which many people object to wearing. Clothes is a verb here, not the garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a refutation, from refute, is a denial that a claim is true.

clue.text: African gnu moved back home

indicators.note: the letters of GNU are shifted out of their places into a new order
going back means read backwards

parts.note: the letters of GNU, rearranged
at home = in, reversed

explanation.surface: A wildebeest has been relocated and returned to its native place.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nguni are a group of southern African peoples, including the Zulu and Xhosa; the word also serves as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional term: Nguni names a family of southern African peoples and languages, so it can stand for African.

clue.text: Cats perhaps united to leave Manx cat on top being playful

indicators.note: to leave is to go away, so U departs from MUSICAL
a Manx cat has no tail, so the word for cat loses its last letter
in a down clue the earlier piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: the cat o' nine tails is a whip; Manx cuts its tail
Cats is a Lloyd Webber musical; U, for United, leaves it

explanation.surface: A cat from the Isle of Man, which has no tail, clambers about playfully among other cats.
explanation.walkthrough: The cat is not a feline but the cat o' nine tails, a whip; Manx cats are famously tailless, hence the dropped P.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something whimsical is fanciful and playfully quaint.

clue.text: Refuse to go to bed, clutching mother's backside

indicators.note: to clutch is to hold tight

parts.note: to doss down is informal British for bedding down to sleep

indicators.note: the rear end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of MOTHER

explanation.surface: A child refuses to go to bed, clinging on to mother's behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Refuse reads as a verb (decline) but is the noun: rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: waste matter, scum on molten metal, is rubbish or refuse.

clue.text: A container filled with a lot of sumptuous fruit

indicators.note: a lot but not all, so RICH loses its last letter

parts.note: as printed
a pot is a container
sumptuous = rich, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A bowl heaped with lavish fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Container is the wordplay's POT, not a hint that the answer holds something.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: the apricot is one kind of stone fruit.

clue.text: Mock funny houses old and irregular

parts.note: to ape is to mimic or mock

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside

parts.note: ridic is slang shortening of ridiculous
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone mocks a comic street of old, irregular houses.
explanation.walkthrough: Houses looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb, and funny is the slangy clipped RIDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical synonym: aperiodic means not recurring at regular intervals.

clue.text: Digital 1980s style newspaper has repeated good article

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
G is short for good, doubling the last letter of RAG
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A trendy digital paper keeps running the same good piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Ragga is a style of Jamaican dancehall music that arose in the 1980s on computerised, digital backing; 'digital' points to the music, not a website.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: this dancehall offshoot was the first Jamaican style built on digital rhythms, in the mid-1980s.

clue.text: Most of trinket left by noble discovered in Belgian city

indicators.note: most but not all, so CHARM loses its last letter
dis-covered, with its cover taken off, so the outside letters go

parts.note: a charm is a trinket, less its last letter
L = left

indicators.note: by means beside, so the next pieces follow on

parts.note: heroic = noble, without its outer H and C

explanation.surface: A small ornament left behind by an aristocrat turns up in a Belgian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Noble is the adjective heroic, not a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper name: this is an industrial city in the Wallonia region of Belgium.

clue.text: Let loose inhaling marijuana in pipe

indicators.note: loose letters are not held in order, so LET can rearrange

parts.note: LET, rearranged
weed is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: Someone lets rip smoking cannabis through a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Pipe is the verb: to tweedle is to play a tune casually on a pipe or fiddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated verb: to tweedle is to play lightly on a pipe, so it means to pipe.

clue.text: Bat possibly in awful fervour biting American soldier

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so FERVOUR is scrambled

parts.note: FERVOUR, rearranged
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A creature in a terrible frenzy sinks its teeth into an American soldier, like a vampire bat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a blood-sucking bat, but the definition is a fruit bat. 'Possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: fruit bats live on fruit, so they are fruit-eaters.

clue.text: Heard horses eat grass

indicators.note: what is heard is spoken, so the word for horses is to be listened to, not read

parts.note: greys are grey horses

explanation.surface: Someone reports horses munching grass.
explanation.walkthrough: A grey is a horse with a white or grey coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: cattle and horses feed on growing grass.

clue.text: Suddenly sees judges backing defendant in the end

indicators.note: to back is to support from behind
the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of DEFENDANT
British judges wear wigs, so wigs stands for them

explanation.surface: In court, the judges realise the defendant is guilty after all.
explanation.walkthrough: Twig is British slang for understand; the surface courtroom supplies WIGS through what judges wear.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: to twig is to catch on, to see the point suddenly.

clue.text: Upset bandaging artillerymen's wound

parts.note: upset = spilled, as of a drink
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Distressed at dressing a gunner's injury.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound is not the injury but the past tense of wind, as a coil is wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A second sense: wound, past tense of wind, means twisted round in coils.

clue.text: Show off skinned fish stuffed with essential piece of peppery rocket prepared here

indicators.note: a skinned thing has lost its outside, so FLAUNT loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to show off is to flaunt, without its outer letters

indicators.note: the essence of a thing is its core, so the middle letter of PEPPERY

parts.note: chad is an old name for the shad, a fish
the middle letter of PEPPERY

explanation.surface: A showy dish of skinned fish stuffed with peppery rocket, the salad leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket reads as a salad leaf beside fish and pepper, but it is a spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the platform from which a rocket is launched is where it is prepared.

clue.text: Peculiar giant pugs stealing the show

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: Some strangely huge pug dogs outshine everyone at a dog show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's show is a dog show; the definition is an idiom for drawing all the attention.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from the theatre: an actor who moves upstage forces others to turn away from the audience.

clue.text: Sport involving bat seemingly made of synthetic material

parts.note: to sport is to play
a stick is used to hit a ball, like a bat

explanation.surface: A game played with a bat that looks cheaply made.
explanation.walkthrough: Sport looks like a noun but is the verb, to play; 'seemingly' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal adjective: looking or feeling like cheap synthetic material.

clue.text: Pass curious monkey driving out east

parts.note: Curious George is the monkey of children's books
E = east, driven out

explanation.surface: An inquisitive monkey drives past, heading out east.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first E of GEORGE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrow valley between hills is a mountain pass.

clue.text: Diver found after craft crosses lake second time

indicators.note: to cross is to span across
coming afterwards, so the seconds and time follow on

parts.note: craft = cunning, guile
L = lake
a mo is a short moment, a second
T = time

explanation.surface: A diver emerges after a boat crosses a lake for the second time.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like a boat but is cunning; the diver is a seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: this auk dives from the sea surface to catch fish.

clue.text: Students outside prying around, ignoring new cleaner

indicators.note: the students stand outside the rest, one at each end
turned around, so NOSY reads backwards
to ignore is to leave out, so N goes

parts.note: L is a learner driver, a student; two of them
prying = nosy, reversed, without N for new

explanation.surface: Nosy students keep snooping round a cleaner who is not new.
explanation.walkthrough: Cleaner looks like a person but is a product: a disinfectant brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand name: this is a household disinfectant, so a cleaner.

clue.text: Seafood and chuck steak 40 per cent off at butcher finally

indicators.note: a discount of 40 per cent takes two of the five letters off STEAK

parts.note: to chuck is to lob
STEAK without its last two letters

indicators.note: the final letter of butcher

parts.note: the last letter of BUTCHER

explanation.surface: A butcher's counter offering chuck steak at a 40 per cent discount, alongside seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Chuck steak is a cut of beef, but chuck is the verb lob.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: this clawed shellfish is a prized seafood.

clue.text: Record holder drawing crowds around made to stand out

indicators.note: to crowd round is to surround

parts.note: drawing is art
c. (circa) = around
hi-vis clothing is made to be highly visible

explanation.surface: A record-breaking act that pulls in crowds and was designed to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Record holder suggests a champion, but it is someone who keeps records.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this person holds and looks after historical records.

clue.text: Mark and Rob sent back box with additional information

indicators.note: sent back the way they came, so the two pieces are read backwards together

parts.note: a pit is a small mark or dent
to loot is to rob

explanation.surface: Two men, Mark and Rob, are returned a parcel with extra notes.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark and Rob look like names. The answer is the small box that pops up when a mouse hovers over something on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A computing term: the pop-up label giving extra information about an on-screen item.

clue.text: Support part of foot cut by machete's tip, vital body part

indicators.note: cut short, so the part of the foot loses its last letter
the tip of a blade is its point, here the first letter of machete

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
the instep is the arched middle of the foot, less its last letter
the first letter of MACHETE

explanation.surface: A supported foot slashed by the point of a machete.
explanation.walkthrough: Cut reads as the machete's slash, but it trims the foot part short.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain description: this link between brain and spinal cord controls breathing, so it is vital.

clue.text: Stocking tiny London stores

indicators.note: to store is to keep inside, so the phrase holds the answer

parts.note: tiNY LONdon

explanation.surface: Small London shops that sell stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: Stores looks like the shops in the surface but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after its material: stockings were so often made of this fibre that the fibre's name became theirs.

clue.text: Cuban steps over tailless snake up ahead

indicators.note: without a tail, so the snake loses its last letter
in a down clue, up is ahead

parts.note: the mamba is an African snake, less its last letter
O = over, as in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Cuban dancing steps over a snake with its tail missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Over is not a position word here but the cricket abbreviation O.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: this Latin dance originated in Cuba.

clue.text: Catch ship having boarded one from Asia

indicators.note: to board is to get on and go inside

parts.note: a Lao is a person from Laos
SS = steamship

explanation.surface: Someone manages to catch the boat after an Asian traveller has got on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship is inside the person, not the other way round: it is the ship that boards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to rope an animal with a noose is to catch it.

clue.text: Monument we should put up on base

indicators.note: to put up is to raise, so in a down clue LETS reads bottom to top

parts.note: let's = let us, a suggestion of what we should do; reversed
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: We ought to raise a monument on a plinth.
explanation.walkthrough: Base looks like a plinth but is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by class: an upright carved stone slab set up as a monument.

clue.text: Examination of cavity without anaesthetic at first

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for anaesthetic is taken away
at first means the start, so the first letter of anaesthetic

parts.words: of cavity without anaesthetic at first
parts.note: atrial means relating to an atrium, a chamber of the heart; A goes

explanation.surface: A dental check-up of a tooth cavity carried out without anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to a dentist, but 'of cavity' is an adjective: the atrium is a cavity of the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a test or hearing, as in a court case, is an examination.

clue.text: Fellow nearly jamming vehicle's wheel?

indicators.note: nearly all, so the word for fellow loses its last letter

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a fellow of a society is a member, less its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone nearly jams a car's wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this cheese comes as a round wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Normandy soft cheese is sold as a small round wheel.

clue.text: Temporary rule in developing Green city's borders

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so GREEN grows into a new order

parts.note: GREEN, rearranged

indicators.note: the borders of a thing are its edges, so the first and last letters of city

parts.note: the first and last letters of CITY

explanation.surface: A temporary planning rule for developing the green belt around a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is rule by a regent while the monarch is a child or unable to reign.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical term: rule by a stand-in for the monarch lasts only until the monarch can reign.

clue.text: After some time leaderless, group of countries quietly gaining more power

indicators.note: without its leader, so the word for time loses its first letter
after means following, so the countries and quietly come behind the first piece

parts.note: a month is a period of time, less its first letter
the European Union
p = piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: A group of nations drifting without a leader for a while quietly grows stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: The group of countries in the surface is also the EU of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something improving or rising is gaining strength.
